clue.text: Perhaps Pulp's Common People, principally describing posh model at the start?

indicators.note: to describe is to draw round, so the first letters of Common and People enclose the rest
principally means taking the chief, leading letter of each of the words Common and People

parts.note: first letter of Common
first letter of People

indicators.note: at the start says the model piece comes first, ahead of the posh letter

parts.note: to hew is to shape or carve, as a sculptor models
U is the old label for upper-class, posh usage

explanation.surface: A question about the Britpop band Pulp and their hit Common People, which is about a posh girl slumming it.
explanation.walkthrough: Pulp's song looks like the subject, but 'Pulp' is a verb here: to chew something up is to reduce it to pulp. 'Perhaps' marks that this is one way of pulping.
explanation.definitionFit: Grinding something with the teeth until it is mashed is one way of reducing it to a pulpy mess.

clue.text: Which person heard laughter and commotion

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: 'which person?' is asking who
ha is the sound of a laugh

explanation.surface: Someone hears a burst of laughter and a fuss breaking out.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoo-ha is an informal word for a noisy fuss or uproar over something.

clue.text: Working under clown car

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the working piece below the clown piece

parts.note: a wag is a joker, a clown
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A circus clown is busy working beneath a clown car.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon is a railway car or carriage for goods, and also a slang word for a car.

clue.text: Agent looks up number, rings immediately — artist volunteers and he's not wanted

indicators.note: looks up in a down clue means the agent word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent

indicators.note: rings means the number word surrounds the immediately word

parts.note: a number is a song
anon is an old word for immediately, at once
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: An agent checks a phone number and calls straight away, while an artist and some volunteers turn up unwelcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Persona non grata is Latin for an unwelcome person, originally a diplomat a country refuses to accept.

clue.text: Shut up about a piece from Toby Young

indicators.note: about means the shut-up word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to immure is to wall up or imprison

indicators.note: a piece from means just the first letter of Toby

parts.note: first letter of Toby

explanation.surface: Someone tells a writer to keep quiet about an article by the journalist Toby Young.
explanation.walkthrough: Toby Young looks like one name, but 'Young' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone young is not yet fully grown or developed, which is what immature means.

clue.text: Very near the batsman, without covering head leading to complaint

indicators.note: without covering means the outside letters of the word are stripped off

parts.note: in cricket, silly describes a fielding position very close to the batsman, as in silly point
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder stands close to the batsman without a helmet, which leads to a grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: SILLY loses its outer letters to leave ILL; NESS is a headland, as in place names like Orford Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint is a common word for an ailment or disorder, so it serves for a sickness.

clue.text: Investing crooked loot in movie that is out before a Tom Cruise film, makes a bomb

indicators.note: before puts the first assembly ahead of the film title
investing means wrapping round, so the shortened movie word encloses the rearranged loot
out after 'that is' means those letters are knocked out of the film word

parts.note: taken as written, then trimmed
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters of loot are rearranged

parts.note: Cocktail is a 1988 film starring Tom Cruise as a bartender

explanation.surface: A tale of a crook putting stolen money into a film that flops, before a Tom Cruise picture becomes a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: MOVIE minus IE is MOV; the anagram of LOOT, OLOT, goes inside to make MOLOTOV. 'Makes a bomb' tempts as box-office slang, but 'bomb' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Molotov cocktail is a crude petrol bomb: a bottle of fuel with a burning rag.

clue.text: Assess what rustlers do

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to review a situation

explanation.walkthrough: Rustlers are thieves who steal cattle, and 'stock' is livestock, so the phrase is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: To take stock is an idiom for pausing to evaluate one's situation, like counting inventory in a shop.

clue.text: About forty days in a little garden, relaxing

parts.note: re means about, concerning
Lent is the forty days of fasting before Easter

indicators.note: a little of the word means only its first letter

parts.note: first letter of garden

explanation.surface: Someone spends about forty days in a small garden, unwinding.
explanation.definitionFit: Relenting means softening or easing off from a harsh stance, as relaxing a rule does.

clue.text: Nonsense from scoundrel drinking gallons — occasionally showing beer belly

indicators.note: drinking means the scoundrel word takes in the gallons letter

parts.note: a dog is a worthless or contemptible fellow

indicators.note: occasionally showing means only every other letter of beer belly appears

explanation.surface: A rogue downing gallons of ale and now and then displaying his paunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters of 'beer belly', starting from the second, give EREL.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggerel is badly written comic verse, so it is used for rubbish or nonsense in rhyme.

clue.text: Kylie dancing after initially lying prone

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged Kylie behind the first letter
initially means the first letter of lying

parts.note: first letter of lying

indicators.note: dancing means the letters of Kylie move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Kylie Minogue dances and then lies flat on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prone' reads as lying face down, matching the surface, but here it means inclined to.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prone to something means being liable or apt to do it, so likely fits.

clue.text: Tropical woodland in outskirts of Rwanda doomed to receive shocking treatment

indicators.note: outskirts means the outer letters of Rwanda, its edge

parts.note: to be in for something is to be bound to get it
EST is electroshock therapy

explanation.surface: Jungle in Rwanda is threatened with brutal handling.
explanation.walkthrough: EST, electroshock therapy, is the less familiar sibling of ECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainforest is dense, wet tropical forest, which is exactly tropical woodland.

clue.text: Smooth navy blue covers

indicators.note: covers means the blue word wraps round the navy letter

parts.note: blue means sad, low

explanation.surface: Smooth navy-blue upholstery or bedding covers.
explanation.definitionFit: To sand wood is to rub it with sandpaper until it is smooth, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Dropping behind, hit good smash — swap ends for service

indicators.note: dropping behind means losing the back, last letter of hit
swap ends means the first and last letters of smash change places

explanation.surface: A tennis player hits a fine smash, then the players change ends before the next serve.
explanation.walkthrough: SMASH with its S and H exchanged gives HMASS. 'Service' sounds like tennis but is a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: High Mass is a Catholic Eucharist celebrated with full ceremony and music, a church service.

clue.text: The exact same form in duplicate — not happy

indicators.note: to form is to shape, so the letters are moulded into a new order
not means the happy letters are left out of the mix

parts.note: up means cheerful, happy

explanation.surface: Filling out a form twice over in exactly the same way, and not pleased about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Take IN DUPLICATE, remove UP, and rearrange INDLICATE to get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that are identical are alike in every detail, the very same.

clue.text: Books troublesome rugby players

parts.note: something hard is difficult, troublesome
the backs are the rugby players behind the scrum

explanation.surface: A referee books some unruly rugby players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Books' looks like a referee's verb, but it is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardbacks are books bound in stiff covers, as opposed to paperbacks.

clue.text: You can play it and see, oddly, if Oslo is Norway's capital?

parts.note: V is short for vide, Latin for see

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters of if Oslo is
capital means the first, head letter of Norway

parts.note: first letter of Norway

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about whether Oslo really is Norway's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A violin is a stringed instrument, something a musician plays with a bow.

clue.text: Eccentric people generally take on board wedding vow

parts.note: we can mean people in general, as in 'we all need sleep'

indicators.note: on board means taken inside, so the vow holds the take letter

parts.note: I do is the vow said at a wedding
R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Most people accept the vows said at a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A weirdo is an odd, unconventional person, so it is a noun for an eccentric.

clue.text: Cake Blog reviewed jam

indicators.note: reviewed suggests looked at again and recast, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A baking blog writes up a review of jam.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam is an obstruction, as in a traffic jam, so it is a stoppage.

clue.text: Singer adopting a retro sound, once overlooked — bless

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the shortened singer word holds the other pieces
overlooked means the word once is ignored and left out

parts.note: Beyoncé is the American singer

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the sound word is read in reverse

parts.note: sound means healthy, fit

explanation.surface: A singer takes up a vintage sound that was once ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: BEYONCE without ONCE leaves BEY, which takes in A plus TIF, FIT turned backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To beatify is for the Pope to declare someone blessed, the step before sainthood.

clue.text: Try second cigarette up north

parts.note: tab is northern English slang for a cigarette

explanation.surface: Someone in the north of England tries a second smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up north' is not a reversal signal here: tab is a cigarette in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a stab at something is an idiom for making an attempt at it.

clue.text: Traditionally the No.1 provider of net protection

definitions.text: Traditionally the No.1 provider of net protection

parts.words: Traditionally the No.1 provider of net protection
parts.note: the player who guards the net in football traditionally wears the number 1 shirt

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a description of an internet security firm; the net is a football goal and No.1 the shirt number.
explanation.definitionFit: The keeper guards the goal net and has traditionally worn the number one jersey in football.

clue.text: Bit part actor from stage, embodying Christ

indicators.note: embodying means holding within its body, so the stage word contains the Christ letter

parts.note: an era is a stage or period of history
Xt is an old written abbreviation for Christ, from the Greek letter chi

explanation.surface: A minor actor in a stage play is cast as Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a film or stage performer hired for a small non-speaking role in a crowd.

clue.text: Projection from First Lady inspiring American society

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the first lady takes in the American letter

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: A speech by a US President's wife that rouses American society.
explanation.walkthrough: First Lady suggests a president's wife, but here it is Eve, the first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaves are the overhanging lower edges of a roof, jutting out beyond the wall.

clue.text: Plant article about spies

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
CA is circa, about
the CIA is the American spy agency

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a spy who has been planted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' could mean an undercover agent, matching the spies, but it is a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The acacia is a thorny tree or shrub, such as the wattle, so it is a plant.

clue.text: During first part of play, venue is empty still

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
Act I is the first part of a play

indicators.note: is empty means the venue loses its insides, keeping only its outer letters

explanation.surface: The theatre is still empty during the first act.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inactive is not moving or working, motionless, which is a sense of still.

clue.text: Celebrity kidnapping fool rejected list of terms

indicators.note: kidnapping means holding captive, so the celebrity word contains the fool

parts.note: glory is fame, celebrity

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the fool word is reversed

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A famous person abducts a fool who then gets turned away from a list.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is an alphabetical list of specialist words with their meanings, often at the back of a book.

clue.text: In Australia I seldom communicate

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone living in Australia confesses they rarely keep in touch.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to cooperate and exchange information with another party, which is communicating.
